text:
alex: Heads-up — saw a weird one during our integration tests. After rotating API keys in CI, a subset of async client requests silently returned 502 and the SDK retried forever (no error surfaced).

maria: oof. do you have a minimal repro? async or sync only?

alex: async only so far. sync client behaves fine. quick repro: start long-running test that instantiates two clients in same process with different env creds. rotate key for CLIENT_A mid-run, some requests from CLIENT_B start hitting 502 but the client just streams blank and never raises.

pjordan: can you paste the init? might be an auth header race or shared session reuse.

alex: here's the pattern (sanitized):
```python
import os
from redwood import AsyncClient

os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'] = 'key_A'
client_a = AsyncClient()

# later in tests, rotate env var
os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'] = 'key_B'
client_b = AsyncClient()
# both clients used concurrently
await client_a.generate(... )  # sometimes 502, no exception
```

maria: hmm looks like AsyncClient() reads globals at import but might be reusing an aiohttp.ClientSession that was created with default header set once. if header mutated the session may be sending stale auth.

syd: +1. also the "silent" part worries me. SDK should raise on non-2xx after retries exhausted. can we add a unit test for this?

alex: reproduction attached in CI gist: https://ci.internal/example/rot-repro (private). logs show repeated 502s but SDK keep attempting.

pjordan: deploy-bot: notify infra?

deploy-bot: @pjordan noted — creating ticket INF-542 to check gateway churn.

maria: proposed fix: make AsyncClient own its own session that freezes auth headers at construction and ensure rotation via explicit client.close() + new client. also make retry logic escalate after N attempts with a clear exception.

syd: agree. tiny UX ask: docs/examples for multi-client usecases. people assume env var changes will affect existing instances. we should add a section under authentication explaining precedence and that clients snapshot creds at init.

alex: patch idea: 1) add explicit warning in docs, 2) change default retry to raise after 3 attempts for 502, 3) ensure session headers are copied on init. I'll draft a PR.

pjordan: can we add a debug flag to surface the underlying http status with the exception? would help customers.

maria: yes. add something like `raise_on_non_2xx=True` at client init or a global debug env `REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG_HTTP=1` that toggles verbose exceptions.

syd: also add a typed error class `AuthenticationError` vs `GatewayError` so users can catch.

alex: will include tests: one that rotates env var, one that creates two async clients and asserts client_a still uses old creds and client_b uses new, and one that checks exception on repeated 502.

pjordan: ping me on the PR. label with "devex:auth" and "bug".

alex: thanks. logging note: in the failing runs we saw no stacktrace because the coroutine awaited a streaming response that never yielded. need a read timeout fallback too.

maria: good call — add a streaming read timeout default (30s) with option to disable.

syd: do we want an internal migration plan? this could affect Dedicated customers who rotate keys via KMS. might need a micro-release.

alex: yep. i'll target a patch release next week. will add upgrade notes: "if you rotate env creds, create new client instances or call client.close()".

maria: awesome. also ping support with repro so they can contact any customer hits.

pjordan: thanks all. I'll add INF-542 as dependent on SDK-781.

alex: quick checklist in the PR description: reproduced in CI, unit tests, new exception types, doc note, read-timeout, change retry default.

syd: :thumbsup:

alex: will follow up with PR link.
